# Sniper

> An open-source HTTP/HTTPS intercepting proxy for macOS and Windows. A desktop
> UI and a JSON-first CLI drive the same local instance, so a person and a coding
> agent can work on the same captured traffic. It is a forward proxy and a
> traffic-inspection layer — not an LLM API gateway and not a reverse proxy.

Sniper captures HTTP, HTTPS and WebSocket traffic from any client configured to
use it, holds requests for editing, replays them, and stores sessions on disk.
The desktop app, `sniper-cli` and an agent all reach the same records through one
local HTTP API. Capture preserves cookies and authorization headers, so anything
reading a capture — including an agent — receives them.

## Docs

- [Debugging HTTP with Sniper](https://smlee.io/Sniper/guides/http-debugging.md): using it as a plain intercepting proxy — starting it, trusting the CA, reading a transaction, scope, replay, and what it does not do
- [Sniper in an agent harness](https://smlee.io/Sniper/guides/agent-harness.md): which part of a harness this is, a worked capture-and-query example, data boundaries, and when you do not need it
- [Using Sniper from Claude Code](https://smlee.io/Sniper/integrations/claude-code.md): installing the bundled skill, confirming it loaded, what to ask for, and the failure modes
- [Using Sniper from Codex](https://smlee.io/Sniper/integrations/codex.md): the same for Codex, including where the two skills differ
- [Architecture](https://smlee.io/Sniper/architecture.md): why it is built this way

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/sm1ee/Sniper): README, install instructions and releases
- [Contributor guide](https://github.com/sm1ee/Sniper/blob/main/AGENTS.md): build, test, persistence invariants and security posture
